source.title: SAEBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Sparse Autoencoders in Language Model Interpretability
source.authors: Adam Karvonen; C. Rager; Johnny Lin; Curt Tigges; J. Bloom; David Chanin; Yeu-Tong Lau; Eoin Farrell; Callum McDougall; K. Ayonrinde; Demian Till; M. Wearden; Arthur Conmy; Samuel Marks; Neel Nanda

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates SAE representations and feature recovery in language models, extending evidence about sparse, distributed features to LLM settings; it does not reproduce the original toy-network method.
record.gate_note: The study measures SAE concept detection, interpretability, absorption, and disentanglement. It does not directly measure superposition geometry, feature-direction angles, or whether neurons are polysemantic because of capacity pressure. Reported choices of L0, intervention budget, and evaluation settings are not separate outcome rows. Findings cited from other work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: A benchmark of SAEs on Gemma-2-2B/9B and Pythia. It bears on V4: SAE latents beat residual-channel and neuron baselines on probing and auto-interp, and SAEs on a random model lose this on supervised metrics. It bears on V5: absorption, and concept isolation that degrades with dictionary width and depends on L0. Its main aim is comparing SAE architectures, so many rows are architecture rankings and bear on no version. It does not reproduce the toy-model setup.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also stress that gains on the sparsity-fidelity proxy do not reliably translate to downstream or disentanglement performance. They say Matryoshka's disentanglement advantage grows with SAE scale. They recommend moderate L0 (50-150) as a compromise across metrics.
record.recipe_differences: The paper benchmarks trained SAEs and measures concept detection, interpretability, reconstruction, and feature disentanglement in LLMs; it does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition setup or measure its geometric transition.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with SAE architecture, dictionary width, L0, intervention budget, layer, and base model. The reported hierarchical-architecture SCR advantage on Gemma-2-2B is absent on Pythia-160M.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025)
record.problems: The authors note limited model and architecture coverage; supervised metrics cover only a small subset of possible concepts and can be noisy; some metrics depend on model capabilities; the unlearning evaluation is limited by Gemma-2-2B performance; and quantitative metrics may not capture qualitative interpretability. Textual summaries often omit exact scores and uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No more than 60 rows were needed. Figure-only detailed values were not transcribed where the text provided no numerical result; the text-described aggregate trends are recorded above.

untested.parts: Toy networks, overlap geometry, the sparsity-dependent phase transition, and regular geometry.
Capacity competition as the cause of polysemanticity; whether important features get dedicated dimensions.
Direct measurement of features being spread across many neurons.
Stability across seeds or runs, and canonicality across SAEs. No ground-truth completeness is measured.
Whether features are 1-D or multi-dimensional. Engels et al. is only cited.

missing.what: Trained vs randomly initialised Pythia-1B SAEs. Random-model SAEs score near or below residual probing on supervised metrics, and only slightly lower on auto-interp. Residual-stream probing gives 94% on the trained model vs 84% on the random one. TPP is higher for random-model SAEs.
Authors note that baseline methods outperform SAEs on several benchmark tasks.

record.verdict_notes: This is an SAE-evaluation benchmark rather than a direct test of superposition. The verdicts rest on the paper's text summaries; exact scores are in the figures only. r10 and r11 also bear on V5 at state partial and are left unchanged. Absorption is measured against linear-probe 'ground truth' directions, so it inherits the probe's assumptions.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network superposition, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether neuron polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
The study evaluates SAE feature recovery and interpretability, but does not measure whether features are spread across many neurons.
The study measures concept detection and several aspects of feature isolation/completeness, but does not test feature stability or whether SAE features are canonical units.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: SAEs evaluated on Gemma-2-2B
rows.size_stated: Gemma-2-2B; SAE widths and architecture vary
rows.operation_detail: Sparse probing of concepts using SAE latents; compared with probing residual-stream channels.

conditions.value: K-sparse; main text focuses on K=1
all evaluated SAEs, aggregate as reported

rows.baseline: Direct probing on K residual-stream channels: 0.65
rows.value: All SAEs significantly outperform the baseline; exact scores not stated.
rows.note: The text reports an aggregate result for all SAEs and does not give individual scores here.

source_check.locator_found: Sections 3.4 and 4.6; Appendix H: Gemma-2-2B layer 12, residual-channel baseline 0.65, main-text K=1.

rows.subject: Gemma-Scope SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Automated interpretability evaluation compared SAE latents with MLP neurons, PCA components, and direct residual-stream readings.
rows.baseline: MLP neuron, PCA, and direct residual-stream baselines
rows.value: SAEs significantly outperform all tested baselines; exact scores not stated.
rows.note: The result concerns interpretability scores for SAE latents, not a direct measurement of feature completeness.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix E, Figure 5 and preceding paragraph; Appendix D, automated interpretability and Table 5.

rows.subject: 65k width ReLU SAEs on Gemma-2-2B
rows.baseline: Other SAE architectures in the evaluated suite
rows.value: ReLU SAEs perform best overall on 1-sparse probing in this L0 range; exact scores not stated.
rows.note: The paper says this result is outside the L0 range typically examined in the literature.
rows.check: Ranks ReLU SAEs above other architectures at L0>200. This is an architecture comparison, not evidence that sparse features exist or are recoverable.

rows.subject: 65k width Gemma-2-2B SAE suite
rows.operation_detail: Compared sparse-probing results as the number of probed latents increased.
rows.value: The SAE advantage over PCA grows substantially as K increases from 1 to 5; exact scores not stated.
rows.note: The authors say this suggests SAEs may capture concepts that require multiple latents.

source_check.correct: PCA is the comparison baseline as K varies through 1, 2 and 5; the reported growing advantage is not a comparison against PCA fixed at K=1.
source_check.locator_found: Appendix H, introductory paragraph and Figure 11.
source_check.problem: The baseline incorrectly fixes PCA at K=1.

rows.subject: 65k width MatryoshkaBatchTopK SAEs on Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Measured feature absorption, reported as the complement of the absorption score.
rows.measure: Feature absorption score (higher complement indicates less absorption)
rows.baseline: Other SAE architectures in the evaluated suite
rows.value: Matryoshka scores best on absorption in the typical L0 range; exact scores not stated.
rows.note: This is a comparative metric result, not evidence that the SAE features are complete or canonical.
rows.check: Says Matryoshka has the least absorption among architectures. A relative ranking cannot show whether SAE features are complete or canonical.

rows.subject: 65k width MatryoshkaBatchTopK SAEs on Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated latent interventions in the RAVEL task.
rows.baseline: Other SAE architectures in the evaluated suite
rows.value: Matryoshka scores best on RAVEL in the typical L0 range; exact scores not stated.
rows.note: The score tests targeted attribute changes and isolation, not feature stability or canonicality.
rows.check: Matryoshka is best on RAVEL among architectures. Relative ranking only.

rows.subject: 65k width MatryoshkaBatchTopK SAEs on Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Zero-ablated selected SAE latents in the Spurious Correlation Removal task.
rows.baseline: Other SAE architectures in the evaluated suite
rows.value: Matryoshka scores best on SCR in the typical L0 range; exact scores not stated.
rows.note: The study identifies this as a feature-disentanglement result.
rows.check: Matryoshka is best on SCR among architectures. Relative ranking only.

rows.subject: 65k width MatryoshkaBatchTopK SAEs on Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Zero-ablated selected SAE latents in the Targeted Probe Perturbation task.
rows.baseline: Other SAE architectures in the evaluated suite
rows.value: Matryoshka scores best on TPP in the typical L0 range; exact scores not stated.
rows.note: This metric measures whether zero-ablation has a targeted effect on selected class probes.
rows.check: Matryoshka is best on TPP among architectures. Relative ranking only.

rows.subject: SAE architectures on Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Compared feature absorption as dictionary width increased.
rows.value: Absorption scores worsen with increased dictionary size for all architectures except Matryoshka, which shows only minor degradation; exact scores not stated.
rows.note: The paper describes this as inverse scaling for most architectures.
rows.check: Absorption worsens with width for all architectures except Matryoshka, so latents do not stably capture a concept as width grows. No absolute absorption values are given in the text.

rows.subject: SAE architectures on Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Compared SCR performance as dictionary width increased at a fixed intervention budget.

conditions.value: fixed number of latents; value not stated
Matryoshka generally improves; most other architectures

rows.value: SCR decreases with scale for most architectures, while Matryoshka generally improves; the pattern persists when intervention size is controlled. Exact scores not stated.
rows.note: The authors consider feature splitting or absorption possible explanations for poorer concept isolation.

rows.subject: Gemma-Scope SAEs
rows.operation_detail: Compared feature-disentanglement metrics across dictionary widths and evaluated layers.
rows.measure: Feature Absorption, SCR, and TPP scores
rows.value: Feature Absorption, SCR, and TPP scores degrade at larger widths; exact values not stated.
rows.note: This is an aggregate trend reported across both model sizes; the text also notes substantial layer-dependent variation.

rows.subject: SAEs on Pythia-160M
rows.operation_detail: Compared the SCR performance of hierarchical and other SAE architectures.
rows.baseline: Other architectures in the Pythia-160M evaluation
rows.value: The hierarchical-architecture advantage on SCR observed for Gemma-2-2B does not appear in Pythia-160M; exact scores not stated.
rows.note: The authors suggest differences in model capabilities may affect supervised metrics.
rows.check: About whether an architecture's advantage carries over to Pythia-160M. It does not measure feature completeness itself.

rows.subject: 65k width Gemma-2-2B SAE suite
rows.operation_detail: Compared disentanglement metrics across L0 values.
rows.baseline: Lower L0 values; exact reference values not stated
rows.value: RAVEL and TPP show a preference for higher L0 values (> 400); the preference is particularly pronounced for TPP. Exact scores not stated.
rows.note: The authors hypothesize that higher sparsity may force multiple concepts into fewer active latents and harm disentanglement.
rows.check: Disentanglement scores depend on the L0 choice, peaking above 400 for TPP and RAVEL, but not for SCR.

relationships.condition: SAEs on trained Gemma-2-2B (layer 12) and the Gemma-Scope SAEs
relationships.reason: All SAEs beat residual-channel probing (0.65); SAE latents beat MLP-neuron, PCA and residual baselines on auto-interp; the SAE advantage over PCA grows with K (r1, r2, r4).
relationships.display_finding: Every SAE beat residual-channel probing (0.65), SAE latents beat MLP-neuron, PCA and residual baselines on auto-interpretability, and the SAE advantage over PCA grew with K.

source_check.reason: Sparse probing exceeds residual-channel probing, automated interpretability exceeds neuron/PCA/residual baselines, and the probing advantage over PCA grows with K.

relationships.condition: Auto-interp metric; SAEs on a randomly initialised Pythia-1B (Appendix E, no row)
relationships.reason: From the text, not the rows: SAEs on a random model score only slightly lower on auto-interp than SAEs on the trained model. So interpretable-looking latents alone do not show the model has learned features. On supervised metrics, random-model SAEs score near or below residual probing.
relationships.display_finding: SAEs on the random model scored only slightly below those on the trained model, so interpretable-looking latents alone do not show that the model learned features. On supervised metrics, random-model SAEs scored near or below residual probing.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Auto-interp metric; SAEs on a randomly initialised Pythia-1B (Appendix E, no row)
source_check.reason: The control limits auto-interpretability's specificity to learned representations. V4 does not assert that specificity; the control does not establish incomplete or failed sparse-feature recovery in trained models.

relationships.condition: Non-hierarchical SAE architectures as dictionary width grows (4k to 65k; Gemma-Scope 16k to 1M), and choice of L0
relationships.reason: Absorption and concept isolation (SCR, TPP) degrade with width; Matryoshka degrades only slightly. Disentanglement depends on L0. Latents are therefore not width-invariant complete units (r9, r10, r11, r13).
relationships.display_finding: Absorption and concept isolation (SCR, TPP) got worse as width grew, while Matryoshka SAEs degraded only slightly. Disentanglement also depended on L0, so latents were not width-invariant units.

relation.reason: Its baseline comparisons and dictionary-scaling results bear directly on V4 and V5.

tranche.reason: Evaluates sparse dictionary recovery and its limitations in trained language models, a different setting from the original toy models.

source_check.notes: Appendix E uses detection-based auto-interpretability. Random-model TPP is higher, with cross-model comparability cautions. Matryoshka generally improves SCR with width; its slight degradation concerns absorption.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Evaluated Gemma-2-2B SAE suite and Gemma-Scope SAEs
reader_labels.reason: SAE latents outperform direct residual-channel probing on sparse probing, and Gemma-Scope SAE latents outperform the tested interpretability baselines (r1–r4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Tested architectures, widths, L0 values, and models
reader_labels.reason: Disentanglement-related outcomes vary by architecture, width, L0, and model; scaling degrades several measures for many architectures, while Matryoshka results are often stronger and the advantage does not generalize to Pythia-160M (r5–r13). The study does not establish completeness, stability, or canonicality.
